title: How we inspect and choose vessels
standfirst: Every vessel on Nilecruz can carry our evaluation: a score out of 100, against the same seven weighted criteria, with the date it was assessed. Here is how it works.

sections.heading: The method
paragraphs: An evaluator scores each vessel on seven dimensions: hygiene, service, food, amenities, management, cabin and vessel, and the cruise experience. Each dimension has four criteria, scored from 0 to 5, and the dimensions are weighted to give a total out of 100. The weights are shown below.

sections.heading: The verdict
paragraphs: With the score comes a verdict: recommended, recommended with reservations, or not recommended. Every evaluation shows the date it was made, so you know how current it is.

sections.heading: What we keep separate
paragraphs: Reviews from other sites are shown with their source and the date we checked them. They are never mixed into our score, and no vessel can pay for its evaluation.

faqs.a: Not yet. A vessel without a published evaluation says so on its page.
Each evaluation shows its date; vessels are evaluated again after changes such as a refit.
